Subject: SIG evidence request — PR gating, CI approvals, ephemeral secrets

Hi Sergio,

AssessCo is scoping FinEdge's SIG-Lite intake and they asked for concrete SDLC evidence focused on PR gating, CI/CD approval flows, and secrets handling for services that process customer data. Can you provide the following artifacts by EOD Monday (2028-03-12)?

- A CSV of PR approvals showing reviewer IDs, approval timestamps, and merge gate enforcement for the last 12 months (redact emails if needed).
- CI run logs for a representative build that demonstrates the approval->deploy workflow and any gates (e.g., manual approval step).
- A short narrative (1 page) describing ephemeral secrets issuance and rotation for CI runners and ephemeral credentials used by deployment pipelines.
- Evidence of change management for emergency hotfixes (approval chain + who issued the keystore rotation if applicable).

If dataset size is large, a secure Drive/S3 link is fine. Also let us know the owner(s) we should call out on the submission.

Thanks — Claire

Claire Mullins

> AssessCo is scoping FinEdge's SIG-Lite intake and they asked for concrete SDLC evidence focused on PR gating, CI/CD approval flows, and secrets handling for services that process customer data. Can you provide the following artifacts by EOD Monday (2028-03-12)?
> ...

--- Attachments delivered (stubs) ---
1) ci-approval-2027Q4.csv (attachment) — CSV columns: pr_id, reviewer_id, review_outcome, approval_ts, merge_ts, branch, repo; redactions applied to reviewer_id to preserve personal data. Sample contains 12 months of production merges for core backend services.

2) pr-guardrails-snapshot.log (attachment) — snapshot of PR enforcement events from git server and webhook logs showing blocked merges when checks failed (lint/test/secret-scan). I included short excerpts with annotated timestamps.

3) ephemeral-secrets-inventory-redacted.json (attachment) — inventory of ephemeral credential families (runner tokens, short-lived KMS grants), their rotation cadence, issuing service, and retention policy. Sensitive token values removed; inventory enumerates key aliases and lifetimes.

4) s3-upload-manifest.txt (attachment) — list of S3 keys where full build logs and longer artifacts are stored; access is restricted via pre-signed URLs which I will generate on request.

Notes / brief narrative:
- PR gating: we enforce branch protection and require two approvals + passing CI checks for prod branches. Automated checks include static analysis, test suite, and secrets-scan (detects hardcoded secrets). Webhook events are logged to the compliance ledger.
- CI approval flow: our pipeline uses a manual approval step for canary and prod deploys (GitHub Actions -> internal approval job -> deploy job). The CSV maps PR -> approval -> deploy timestamps and demonstrates enforcement.
- Ephemeral secrets: CI runners obtain short-lived credentials via our internal IAM service which mints database and KMS grants with TTLs <= 1 hour. Rotations are automatic at renewal; long-lived secrets are stored only in KMS with strict access controls.
- Emergency hotfixes: hotfixes go through an expedited approval path that still records approver identity; keystore rotations are recorded in the change log and coordinated with Security.

If AssessCo would like, I can produce a redacted timeline for one representative hotfix showing who approved and the keystore rotation commit.

Best,
